verses.greek: Κἀγώ, ἀδελφοί, οὐκ ἠδυνήθην λαλῆσαι ὑμῖν ὡς πνευματικοῖς ἀλλʼ ὡς σαρκίνοις, ὡς νηπίοις ἐν Χριστῷ.
verses.literal: And I myself brothers not was able to speak to you as to spiritual but as to fleshly as to infants in Christ.
verses.dgt: And I, brothers and sisters, was not able to speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to fleshly people, as to infants in Christ.

verses.greek: γάλα ὑμᾶς ἐπότισα, οὐ βρῶμα, οὔπω γὰρ ἐδύνασθε. ἀλλʼ οὐδὲ ἔτι νῦν δύνασθε,
verses.literal: Milk you I gave to drink not solid food not yet for were you able In fact not still now are you able
verses.dgt: I gave you milk to drink, not solid food, for you were not yet able. Indeed, even now you are still not able,

verses.greek: ἔτι γὰρ σαρκικοί ἐστε. ὅπου γὰρ ἐν ὑμῖν ζῆλος καὶ ἔρις, οὐχὶ σαρκικοί ἐστε καὶ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον περιπατεῖτε;
verses.literal: still for fleshly you are. Where for are among you jealousy and strife surely fleshly are you and according to man are walking?
verses.dgt: for you are still fleshly. For when jealousy and strife are among you, are you not fleshly and walking according to human ways?

verses.greek: ὅταν γὰρ λέγῃ τις· Ἐγὼ μέν εἰμι Παύλου, ἕτερος δέ· Ἐγὼ Ἀπολλῶ, οὐκ ἄνθρωποί ἐστε;
verses.literal: When for may say one I myself indeed am of Paul another however I myself of Apollos surely human are you?
verses.dgt: For whenever someone says, “I am of Paul,” and another, “I am of Apollos,” are you not merely human?

verses.greek: Τί οὖν ἐστιν Ἀπολλῶς; τί δέ ἐστιν Παῦλος; διάκονοι διʼ ὧν ἐπιστεύσατε, καὶ ἑκάστῳ ὡς ὁ κύριος ἔδωκεν.
verses.literal: who then is Apollos who now is Paul Servants through whom you believed also to each as the Lord has given.
verses.dgt: What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? Servants through whom you believed, as the Lord gave to each.

verses.greek: ἐγὼ ἐφύτευσα, Ἀπολλῶς ἐπότισεν, ἀλλὰ ὁ θεὸς ηὔξανεν·
verses.literal: I myself planted Apollos watered but the God was it growing
verses.dgt: I planted, Apollos watered, but God was causing the growth.

verses.greek: ὥστε οὔτε ὁ φυτεύων ἐστίν τι οὔτε ὁ ποτίζων, ἀλλʼ ὁ αὐξάνων θεός.
verses.literal: So neither the one planting is anything nor the one watering but only the One giving growth — God
verses.dgt: So then neither the one planting is anything nor the one watering, but God who causes the growth.

verses.greek: ὁ φυτεύων δὲ καὶ ὁ ποτίζων ἕν εἰσιν, ἕκαστος δὲ τὸν ἴδιον μισθὸν λήμψεται κατὰ τὸν ἴδιον κόπον,
verses.literal: The one planting now also the one watering one are each now the his own reward will receive according to the his own labor.
verses.dgt: Now the one planting and the one watering are one, but each will receive their own reward according to their own labor.

verses.greek: θεοῦ γάρ ἐσμεν συνεργοί· θεοῦ γεώργιον, θεοῦ οἰκοδομή ἐστε.
verses.literal: Of God for we are fellow workers God’s field God’s building you are.
verses.dgt: For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s field, God’s building.

verses.greek: Κατὰ τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι ὡς σοφὸς ἀρχιτέκτων θεμέλιον ἔθηκα, ἄλλος δὲ ἐποικοδομεῖ. ἕκαστος δὲ βλεπέτω πῶς ἐποικοδομεῖ·
verses.literal: According to the grace the of God which having been given to me as a wise master builder the foundation I laid another however is building upon it. Each one however should take heed how he builds upon it.
verses.dgt: According to the grace of God given to me, like a wise master builder I laid a foundation, and another builds on it. But let each one watch how they build on it.

verses.greek: θεμέλιον γὰρ ἄλλον οὐδεὶς δύναται θεῖναι παρὰ τὸν κείμενον, ὅς ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός·
verses.literal: Foundation for another no one is able to lay besides the one being already laid which is Jesus Christ.
verses.dgt: For no one can lay another foundation besides the one laid, which is Jesus Christ.

verses.greek: εἰ δέ τις ἐποικοδομεῖ ἐπὶ τὸν θεμέλιον χρυσόν, ἄργυρον, λίθους τιμίους, ξύλα, χόρτον, καλάμην,
verses.literal: If now anyone builds upon the foundation gold silver stones precious wood hay straw
verses.dgt: Now if anyone builds on the foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, grass, straw,

verses.greek: ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον φανερὸν γενήσεται, ἡ γὰρ ἡμέρα δηλώσει· ὅτι ἐν πυρὶ ἀποκαλύπτεται, καὶ ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον ὁποῖόν ἐστιν τὸ πῦρ αὐτὸ δοκιμάσει.
verses.literal: of each the work manifest will become the for day will disclose it because in fire it is revealed and of each the work what sort it is the fire itself will prove.
verses.dgt: the work of each will become evident, for the day will make it clear, because it is revealed in fire; and the fire itself will test what sort of work each person has.

verses.greek: εἴ τινος τὸ ἔργον μενεῖ ὃ ἐποικοδόμησεν, μισθὸν λήμψεται·
verses.literal: If of anyone the work will remain which he built up a reward he will receive
verses.dgt: If anyone’s work that they built remains, they will receive a reward.

verses.greek: εἴ τινος τὸ ἔργον κατακαήσεται, ζημιωθήσεται, αὐτὸς δὲ σωθήσεται, οὕτως δὲ ὡς διὰ πυρός.
verses.literal: If of anyone the work will be burned up he will suffer loss he himself however will be saved so however as through fire.
verses.dgt: If anyone’s work is burned up, they will suffer loss, but they themselves will be saved, yet so as through fire.

verses.greek: Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ναὸς θεοῦ ἐστε καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν;
verses.literal: Surely you know that temple of God you yourselves are and the Spirit the of God dwells in you
verses.dgt: Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?

verses.greek: εἴ τις τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ φθείρει, φθερεῖ τοῦτον ὁ θεός· ὁ γὰρ ναὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ἅγιός ἐστιν, οἵτινές ἐστε ὑμεῖς.
verses.literal: If anyone the temple the of God destroys will destroy him the God the for the temple the of God holy is which are you yourselves.
verses.dgt: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy that person; for God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.

verses.greek: Μηδεὶς ἑαυτὸν ἐξαπατάτω· εἴ τις δοκεῖ σοφὸς εἶναι ἐν ὑμῖν ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ, μωρὸς γενέσθω, ἵνα γένηται σοφός,
verses.literal: No one himself should deceive if anyone thinks himself wise to be among you in the age this foolish he should become so that he may become wise.
verses.dgt: Let no one deceive themselves. If anyone among you thinks they are wise in this age, let them become foolish so that they may become wise.

verses.greek: ἡ γὰρ σοφία τοῦ κόσμου τούτου μωρία παρὰ τῷ θεῷ ἐστιν· γέγραπται γάρ· Ὁ δρασσόμενος τοὺς σοφοὺς ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτῶν·
verses.literal: The for wisdom of the world this foolishness with the God is. It has been written for: He is the One catching the wise in the craftiness of them
verses.dgt: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, “He catches the wise in their craftiness,”

verses.greek: καὶ πάλιν· Κύριος γινώσκει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς τῶν σοφῶν ὅτι εἰσὶν μάταιοι.
verses.literal: And again The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise that they are futile.
verses.dgt: and again, “The Lord knows the reasonings of the wise, that they are futile.”

verses.greek: ὥστε μηδεὶς καυχάσθω ἐν ἀνθρώποις· πάντα γὰρ ὑμῶν ἐστιν,
verses.literal: Therefore no one should boast in men All things for of you are
verses.dgt: So then let no one boast in people. For all things are yours,

verses.greek: εἴτε Παῦλος εἴτε Ἀπολλῶς εἴτε Κηφᾶς εἴτε κόσμος εἴτε ζωὴ εἴτε θάνατος εἴτε ἐνεστῶτα εἴτε μέλλοντα, πάντα ὑμῶν,
verses.literal: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or things being present or things to come — all yours
verses.dgt: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or things present or things coming—all are yours,

verses.greek: ὑμεῖς δὲ Χριστοῦ, Χριστὸς δὲ θεοῦ.
verses.literal: you now of Christ Christ now of God.
verses.dgt: and you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.
